item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
834
ABPZ20 KNHC 031716
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Thu Sep 3 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Karina, located well east of the Hawaiian Islands, on Hurricane
Lowell, located several hundred miles south of the Hawaiian Islands,
and on Hurricane Marie, located several hundred miles southwest of
the southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of low pressure could form well offshore of southwestern
Mexico early next week. Gradual development is possible, and the
system could become a tropical depression around the middle of next
week while it moves west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph, likely
remaining well offshore of Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...40 percent.

$$
Forecaster Reinhart/Evans

WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 1100 AM HST (2100 UTC), the center of Hurricane Karina was
located near latitude 19.8 North, longitude 137.6 West. Karina is
moving toward the west near 10 mph (17 km/h), and a turn toward 
the west-northwestward is expected over the next couple of days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 105 mph (165 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Weakening is expected to continue over the next 48 hours, 
although Karina is expected to remain a hurricane during the next 
day or two.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 40 miles (65 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 125 miles
(205 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 969 mb (28.62 inches).

item.title: Hurricane Karina Forecast Discussion Number 30
item.description:
Issued at 1100 AM HST Thu Sep 03 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 032031
TCDEP1
 
Hurricane Karina Discussion Number  30
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
1100 AM HST Thu Sep 03 2026
 
Karina's cold cloud tops around the center appear more  
asymmetrical on satellite imagery, with dry air wrapping into the 
system. The latest subjective Dvorak analysis from TAFB gave an 
intensity estimate of 90 kt, while objective estimates from CIMSS 
ranged from 90-95 kt. With Dvorak analyses continuing to trend 
downward, along with Karina's degraded appearance on satellite 
imagery, the initial intensity estimate was decreased to 90 kt.
 
Karina's initial motion was set slightly more westward at 275/9 kt.
The system continues to be guided by a subtropical ridge to its
north, but is still expected to turn more west-northwestward
into the weekend as an upper-level trough moves in and weakens the 
aforementioned ridge. Another complicating factor for Karina's 
track is for it to potentially interact with Lowell early next 
week, which may pull Karina a bit more westward than the last 
advisory had suggested. Global models seem to hint at this
possibility, so the latest official track forecast reflects a
slight westward shift, however Karina is not expected to be a 
threat to the main Hawaiian Islands.
 
The environment surrounding Karina is becoming increasingly drier
based on latest SHIPS guidance, which should induce weakening 
in the short term. Marginal SSTs and increasing vertical
wind shear are forecast to cause additional weakening over the 
weekend. Karina is expected to become a post-tropical system by 
Monday, before dissipating thereafter. The official NHC intensity 
forecast further hastens the rate of weakening, generally falling 
close to the consensus aids.

item.description:

BULLETIN
Hurricane Marie Advisory Number  10
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
800 AM MST Thu Sep 03 2026
 
...MARIE A LITTLE STRONGER...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM MST...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...19.2N 114.9W
ABOUT 410 MI...660 KM SW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...90 MPH...150 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 290 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...976 MB...28.82 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM MST (1500 UTC), the center of Hurricane Marie was located 
near latitude 19.2 North, longitude 114.9 West. Marie is moving 
toward the west-northwest near 10 mph (17 km/h), and this motion is 
expected to continue through this weekend.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 90 mph (150 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Some strengthening is forecast over the next day or so, 
followed by gradual weakening this weekend.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 40 miles (65 km) from the 
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 230 miles 
(370 km). The Mexican Navy Weather Station on Clarion Island 
recently reported a wind gust of 56 mph (90 km/h) in one of Marie's 
outer rain bands. 
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 976 mb (28.82 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Marie will affect portions of the coast of
southwest Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula for the next few
days and will likely spread northward to Southern California over
the weekend. These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf
and rip current conditions. Please consult products from your local
weather office. A depiction of rip current risk for the United
States can be found at:
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?ripCurrents
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM MST.
 
$$
Forecaster Adams

item.title: Hurricane Marie Forecast Discussion Number 10
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM MST Thu Sep 03 2026 
629 
WTPZ43 KNHC 031449
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Marie Discussion Number  10
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
800 AM MST Thu Sep 03 2026
 
The structure of Marie has improved this morning. First-light 
visible satellite imagery shows convection becoming increasingly 
symmetric around the hurricane's center, with colder cloud tops 
wrapping nearly completely around the core. The latest Dvorak 
intensity estimate from TAFB was 4.5/77 kt, while objective 
intensity estimates range from 68-83 kt. Given the improved 
satellite presentation and upward trend in intensity estimates, the 
initial intensity has been set at 80 kt for this advisory. 
 
Marie is moving west-northwestward around 9 kt, guided by a 
mid-level ridge to its northwest. This general motion is expected to 
continue over the next 2-3 days. By late this weekend into next 
week, however, considerable spread develops in the track guidance as 
the aforementioned ridge weakens and an upper-level low approaches 
the West Coast of the United States. The strength of this low could 
have a significant influence on Marie's long-range track. A stronger 
system moving into the western U.S. would erode the ridge more 
substantially and result in a more northward track, while a weaker 
system would allow the ridge to remain stronger and keep Marie on a 
more west-northwestward heading. Given these uncertainties, 
confidence in the track forecast is somewhat lower than normal. The 
latest NHC forecast is similar to the previous track and remains 
very close to the Google Deep Mind and HCCA solutions through 60 h. 
Thereafter, the forecast has been nudged to the right of the 
previous track through the remainder of the forecast period. 

The hurricane is moving through warm waters around 28-29 C in an 
environment with low wind shear, moist mid-level air and favorable 
upper-level divergence. These conditions are expected to persist 
over the next 24-36 h, and Marie is forecast to gradually 
strengthen. It is worth noting that the ECMWF and GFS SHIPS guidance 
indicate a small potential for rapid intensification during this 
period, and because of this, the official NHC forecast intensity 
remains near the top of the guidance envelope. The medium- to 
long-range intensity forecast will depend strongly on Marie's track. 
A more northward track would allow the hurricane to remain in 
slightly warmer waters for a longer period, while a more 
west-northwestward track would bring Marie over cooler waters and 
likely result in a faster rate of weakening. The official NHC 
intensity forecast calls for Marie to begin slowly weakening this 
weekend as increasing mid-level dry air wraps around the hurricane, 
with a more steady rate of weakening expected early next week.
